newsitem.title: UK: German official says road to EMU will be bumpy.
newsitem.headline: German official says road to EMU will be bumpy.

text.p: The road to European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) may still prove rough for those wishing to take it, a German finance official said on Wednesday.

Speaking in an unofficial capacity, Rolf Guenther Thumann of the German Federal Ministry for Economics said public opinion, high unemployment, fiscal laxity and an unclear stability pact may present difficulties for a single currency.
"There are still a number of potholes on the road to EMU-land -- so the journey may be bumpy," Thumann told delegates at an EMU conference in London.
"But pointing out the risks of going to EMU-land doesn't suggest that we shouldn't go there," he said.
He said it was important that the convergence criteria laid down in the Maastricht Treaty were strictly adhered to when the decision was made on who is to be in and who is to be out.

"There are deep-seated concerns in Germany about (the possibility of) inflation and the stability of the euro," he said -- adding that the one key to a successful EMU would be a firm hand by the the European Central Bank in the early years.
"They must not lose credibility at the start," he said, calling for prudent European monetary policy to ensure the risk of inflation was kept at bay.
Thumann stessed that European nations should heed the problems facing EMU and warned against over-optimism that the programme would go ahead on time.
"The chances of a core Euro are more than even, but I would say that EMU is not a done deal yet," he said.
